tldr:
For exact equality of marginal counterfactual categorical laws, the simultaneous original-record minimax sample complexity under known uniform strata and unknown assignments to propensity levels \(\{1/4,3/4\}\) is of order
\[
F(d,k,\epsilon)=\max\left\{k^{2/3}\epsilon^{-4/3},\sqrt{k}\epsilon^{-2},(dk/\epsilon^2)^{2/5},\sqrt d\,k^{1/4}/\epsilon\right\}.
\]
A total finite bounded-bit test attains this order, and exact-null full-record priors give the matching converse. Supplying the propensity vector reduces the order to the inherited categorical benchmark \(B(k,\epsilon)\). The evaluated ratio \(F/B\) describes the unknown-assignment penalty, which diverges exactly when \(d/B\) diverges. The null permits arbitrary stratum-level effects to cancel; the theorem has no logarithmic factors.
